tools.title: AWS

servers.name: AWS MCP Server
servers.capabilities: Call AWS APIs across services with IAM permissions and CloudTrail logging, search AWS documentation and follow Agent SOPs.
servers.access: Read or write, depending on the server configuration, the tools enabled or the consent given.
servers.scopes: AWS IAM actions and resources granted to the session. Consent: Connect with an authorized AWS identity.

tools.notes: Regional endpoints also in us-west-2, ap-southeast-1/2, ap-northeast-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2. OAuth needs the AWSMCPSignInOAuthAccessPolicy; SigV4 via `uvx mcp-proxy-for-aws-cli@latest <endpoint>`. Preview status taken from the awslabs/mcp README; awslabs also publishes many per-service local servers.

tools.title: Microsoft Azure

servers.name: Azure MCP Server
servers.capabilities: Manage and query Azure resources (storage, Cosmos DB, Key Vault, monitoring, AKS and more) using the signed-in Azure identity.
servers.scopes: Azure RBAC roles and resource scope of the signed-in identity. Consent: Sign in locally with an authorized Azure identity.

read_only.how: The --read-only flag exposes only read tools.

tools.notes: Azure MCP Server 2.0 is generally available. It authenticates with your local Azure credentials (for example Azure CLI sign-in); also published on NuGet and PyPI.

tools.title: Cloudflare
tools.summary: Edge network, CDN, security and developer platform (Workers, R2, DNS).

servers.name: Cloudflare API MCP Server
servers.capabilities: Access the whole Cloudflare API (about 2,500 endpoints) through code mode tools.
servers.access: Read or write, depending on the server configuration, the tools enabled or the consent given.

tools.notes: Cloudflare also hosts product-specific servers (docs, observability, browser, containers, audit logs...) listed in cloudflare/mcp-server-cloudflare, and asks users of the deprecated ones to migrate to this API server. Token auth uses a Cloudflare API token as Bearer.

tools.title: Docker
tools.summary: Container build and runtime tooling (Docker Engine, Docker Desktop); Docker Hub is the docker-hub tool.

servers.name: Docker MCP Gateway
servers.capabilities: Single MCP endpoint that runs and proxies containerised MCP servers from the Docker MCP Catalog, with secrets and OAuth handling.
servers.access: Read or write, depending on the server configuration, the tools enabled or the consent given.
servers.scopes: Permissions depend on the enabled servers and their credentials. Consent: Configure the enabled servers and authorize each upstream connection separately.

tools.notes: This is a gateway to other MCP servers, not a server for managing Docker itself; it needs Docker Desktop 4.59+ with MCP Toolkit enabled, or the docker-mcp CLI plugin. No official Docker-management MCP server was found.

tools.title: Google Cloud

servers.name: gcloud MCP server
servers.capabilities: Run gcloud CLI commands from the agent to manage Google Cloud resources.

servers.name: Cloud Run remote MCP server
servers.capabilities: Read Cloud Run services, revisions and logs, and deploy services with the signed-in user's Cloud Run permissions.
servers.scopes: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/run.readonly for read access; https://www.googleapis.com/auth/run for read and write access. Consent: Use a Google Cloud identity with the MCP Tool User role and the required Cloud Run IAM permissions.

tools.notes: Uses the local gcloud credentials. Google also hosts remote MCP servers per product (e.g. GKE https://container.googleapis.com/mcp, Compute Engine https://compute.googleapis.com/mcp, Logging https://logging.googleapis.com/mcp, Monitoring https://monitoring.googleapis.com/mcp), governed by IAM.

tools.title: Kubernetes

servers.name: Kubernetes MCP Server
servers.capabilities: Manage pods, resources, Helm releases, events and logs across clusters defined in kubeconfig or in-cluster config.
servers.scopes: Kubernetes RBAC for the selected identity, namespaces and resources. Consent: Set the intended kubeconfig context or configure an in-cluster service account.

read_only.how: The --read-only flag exposes only read tools.

tools.notes: No MCP server published by the Kubernetes project was found. This community server (about 2,270 stars, commits on 2026-11-20) uses the local kubeconfig credentials; also on PyPI.

tools.title: Netlify
tools.summary: Web platform to build, deploy and host sites and apps.

servers.name: Netlify MCP Server (remote)
servers.capabilities: Create, build, deploy and manage Netlify projects, environment variables, forms and extensions.

servers.name: Netlify MCP Server (local)
servers.capabilities: Same capabilities run locally; needs Node.js 22+.

tools.notes: Netlify recommends the remote server; the previous URL https://netlify-mcp.netlify.app/mcp still works. The docs do not name the remote transport (streamable-http assumed). The repository shows no licence.

tools.title: Terraform
tools.summary: Infrastructure as code, with HCP Terraform and Terraform Enterprise.

servers.name: Terraform MCP Server
servers.capabilities: Search Terraform Registry providers and modules, manage HCP Terraform/Terraform Enterprise workspaces, runs and private registry.

servers.name: Terraform MCP Server (hosted)
servers.capabilities: Hosted version of the same server, authenticated with an HCP Terraform token as Bearer.

tools.notes: TFE_TOKEN and TFE_ADDRESS are only needed for HCP Terraform/Terraform Enterprise tools; registry search works without them. The README passes them as -e NAME=value; here the variables are passed from the environment.

tools.title: Vercel
tools.summary: Frontend cloud for deploying web apps and serverless functions.

servers.name: Vercel MCP
servers.capabilities: Search Vercel docs, manage teams, projects and deployments, read deployment logs and query Web Analytics.

tools.notes: Available on all plans; only reviewed clients or clients using CIMD can connect.
